acceptance: The decision is recorded with the reasoning.
If a gate is added, it follows the billable guard's pattern (flag plus environment variable, documented exit code from benchbox/cli/exit_codes.py) and has tests.
Whether a non-maintainer can set the trust label maintainer-run on publish is checked and either restricted or documented.
context:
Source: found on 2026-11-13 while delivering the agent-facing work (PRs BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4202, #4203 and BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site#152, #153, #154). Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items share one feature branch and PR where their files overlap. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy and add a changelog.d fragment for user-facing changes. Re-verify every cited file and line before acting; they are hints. Stop and report rather than widen scope.

Owner decision (2026-11-14): gate hosted submission and restrict the label. submit --service refuses non-interactively without an explicit acknowledgement (flag plus environment variable, reusing exit code 6 ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_REQUIRED from benchbox/cli/exit_codes.py). publish refuses the maintainer-run trust label unless an environment variable explicitly allows it. Local and storage publication are otherwise unchanged.

Closeout (2026-11-14): https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4229 merged (3f8cf88f4a). ~/.benchbox is created 0700 and credentials.yaml written through a 0600 temporary file and renamed; failure raises; wider files are tightened with a warning; ${VAR} references are no longer written back as plaintext; README documents plaintext storage. submit --service exits 6 non-interactively without --acknowledge-hosted-submission or BENCHBOX_ACKNOWLEDGE_HOSTED_SUBMISSION=1; publish refuses the maintainer-run label (the default, so a breaking change) unless BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAINTAINER_LABEL=1. setup --remove (new --yes), export overwrite and publish remove exit 6 when no answer can be read; run --non-interactive reaches the orchestrator as non-interactive; publish help fixed. Both gates state intent; they are not access control.
description:
Problem: with BENCHBOX_SUBMIT_TOKEN or BENCHBOX_SERVICE_TOKEN set, or a token in the keyring, `benchbox submit --service` uploads to the hosted corpus with no confirmation; `auth login --token-stdin` stores a token non-interactively. `benchbox publish run` and `run --publish` copy bundles to any local, s3, gs or abfss destination with ambient cloud credentials, with a caller-chosen trust label defaulting to maintainer-run. An agent with those credentials can publish without a human step. Admission still refuses unclean or unofficial results.

Outcome: an owner decision on whether hosted submission and remote publication need an explicit acknowledgement or a human-issued token scope, then the change or the documentation.
